entries.title: Proverbs 15:2
segments:
CHAP. XV. 
 
  V. 2. Aright-Expressing what he knows prudently and gracefully. Poureth out-Plentifully, continually, and vehemently, as a fountain does waters.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:4
segments: V. 4. Wholesome-Which utters sound and useful counsels.  Tree of life-Is greatly useful to preserve the present life, and to promote the spiritual and eternal life, both of the speaker and hearers. Perverseness-False or corrupt speeches.  A breach-Disturbs and wounds the spirits, both of the speaker and hearers.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:6
segments: V. 6. Revenues-Though he may obtain great revenues, yet they are attended with much trouble.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:7
segments: V. 7. Disperse-Freely communicate to others what they know.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:8
segments: V. 8. Sacrifice-All the religious services, yea, the most costly; one kind being put for all the rest.  Prayer-The cheapest and meanest services.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:11
segments: V. 11. Destruction-The place of destruction, of which men know nothing but by Divine revelation.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:14
segments: V. 14. Foolishness-Wickedness is meat and drink to them.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:15
segments: V. 15. Afflicted-Of the troubled in mind.  Evil-Tedious and uncomfortable.  Chearful-Heb. of a good heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:16
segments: V. 16. Trouble-Tumultuous lusts and passions, vexatious cares, and horrors of conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:19
segments: V. 19. An hedge-As a way hedged up with thorns, troublesome, perplexed, and full of difficulties.  Plain-Is easy and pleasant to him, notwithstanding all its difficulties.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:22
segments: V. 22. Counsel-When men do not seek, or will not receive advice from others.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:23
segments: V. 23. The answer-By a wise, or good and seasonable answer.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:24
segments: V. 24. The way-The way a wise man takes to obtain life, is to place his heart, and treasure, and conversation on things above.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:25
segments: V. 25. The proud-Of the mighty oppressors.  The border-The estate, the border being often used, for the land within the borders.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:26
segments: V. 26. Pleasant-Acceptable to God.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:27
segments: V. 27. Troubleth-Brings God's curse upon himself and family. Gifts-Bribes given to corrupt judgment.  Live-Shall preserve himself and family from ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:28
segments: V. 28. Studieth-He speaks considerately.  The mouth-Not the heart; for he rashly speaks what comes into his mouth, without the direction of his heart or conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:30
segments: V. 30. A good report-A good name.  Fat-Not only chears a man for the present, but gives him such stable comfort as revives his soul, and gives vigour to his body.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:31
segments: V. 31. The ear-The man that hearkens to that reproof which leads to life, seeks and delights in the company of the wise.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:33
segments: V. 33. The instruction-Doth instruct men in true wisdom.
